one_paragraph_summary: The engineering underneath FINDING 18 is the cleanest I have reviewed in this programme: I recomputed 108 numbers from the two tables against the source JSONs and found exactly one disagreement, and that one is a round-half tie (4.81940 - 4.79455 = 0.024850, printed 0.0249). The controls are real and they pass at machine precision (C1 loop-transcription difference exactly 0.0 held nats; C3 naive fp64 reference 4.3e-16; C5 causality 0.0; C7 family retrained-now drift 0.0 nats; C4 probe-shim reproduction abs_diff exactly 0.0). Parameter matching is exact and it is exact at BOTH levels, not just body: at all nine cells the x7 arm's live n_params equals the family's live n_params to the integer (598,080 / 1,343,616 / 3,277,056 / 671,872 / 1,638,656 / 4,456,960 / 745,664 / 1,933,696 / 5,636,864) and body_params likewise. The two families are probed by literally the same function with the same defaults (n_seq=48, L=96, probe seeds 0-4) on bit-identical synthetic inputs, so the induction numbers are commensurable. The cross-entropy tax and the direction and size of the induction gap therefore survive. What does NOT survive is the specific framing of the headline. (1) The one-octave THRESHOLD clause is criterion-dependent in precisely the way FINDING 16, in the same file, already retracted once: of the three criteria FINDING 16 itself constructed, only one gives 'one octave at every depth >= 2'; the model-seed criterion FINDING 16 explicitly ADOPTED gives no shift at depth 2 (conventional d2w128 model-seed t = 2.56, below both the 3.182 bar FINDING 16 used and the 4.30 bar this finding's own report code uses), and FINDING 16's 20-probe-seed criterion puts the FAMILY at width 64 at depth 3, which removes the depth-3 shift. FINDING 16 also adopted, in writing, 'the programme should stop quoting a threshold as the headline'; FINDING 18's headline is a threshold. (2) The depth-3 family column is seed 0 only, and the text's justification ('three model seeds at depths 1-2, one at depth 3') is factually wrong -- all three depth-3 family seeds are on disk, are already aggregated in this finding's own tf_baseline_std.json, and were already PUBLISHED as a three-seed surface in FINDING 16 section 3. Using them moves the quoted multipliers from 6.4x to 5.4x (depth 3 width 128) and from 5.2x to 3.7x (depth 3 width 256). (3) The x7 arm that carries the bolded tax range is single-seed at every cell. The good news for the finding is that a criterion-FREE restatement is available from data already on disk and is stronger than the threshold claim: over three family model seeds the family's synthetic induction score is bounded above by +0.0138 at depth 2 width 128 and +0.0106 at depth 3 width 64 (mean + 3 model-seed SE), against conventional two-seed means of +0.1356 and +0.1365 -- a 10x and 13x separation that no choice of threshold can undo, and the family needs at least one octave more width to reach the conventional model's score at every depth >= 2.

objections.target: "a conventional softmax+GELU transformer crosses the induction floor **one octave of width earlier at every depth >= 2**" and "**2. The threshold shift is exactly one octave, at both depths where a threshold exists.**"
objections.objection: FINDING 16, six sections down the same RESULTS.md, retracted a width-threshold claim because it was 'a property of the detection criterion, not of the model', and it ADOPTED two rules in writing: (a) 'a threshold claim must be defined over MODEL seeds', and (b) 'the programme should stop quoting a threshold as the headline. The defensible object is the continuous magnitude surface.' FINDING 18's headline is a threshold claim and its inducts/no columns are decided against a floor defined over PROBE seeds -- the exact criterion FINDING 16 retracted. This is the 'reinstating a retracted inference without redoing the check that retracted it' standing failure mode, applied to the very finding that established the retraction.
objections.what_I_measured: I rebuilt the threshold pair (depth 2, depth 3) for both families under seven criteria computed from the JSONs on disk: (C1) FINDING 18's published table criterion (score > its floor); (C1p) score > mean planted-oracle power floor; (C2) one-sample t over MODEL seeds > 4.30, the bar hard-coded as MODEL_SEED_T_BAR in this finding's own tf_baseline_report.py; (C3) t over model seeds > 3.0 (and separately > 3.182, FINDING 16's t(2) bar -- same answers); (C4) fixed absolute threshold 0.05 nats; (C5) EVERY model seed clears its own 3-SE-over-probe-seeds floor; (C6) every model seed clears its own planted-oracle power floor. Family n=3 model seeds at all nine cells; conventional x4 n=2; conventional x7 n=1.
objections.result: Thresholds (depth2/depth3), family vs conventional-x4:  C1 256/128 vs 128/64 (one octave at both depths).  C1p 256/128 vs 128/64 (one octave).  C4 abs>0.05 256/128 vs 128/64 (one octave).  C5 256/128 vs 128/64 (one octave).  C6 256/128 vs 128/64 (one octave).  C2 (t>4.30, the programme's own registered bar) 256/128 vs 256/128 -- NO SHIFT AT EITHER DEPTH.  C3 (t>3.0 or t>3.182) 256/128 vs 256/64 -- no shift at depth 2, one octave at depth 3. The decisive numbers are the conventional model-seed t values at the two cells that define the shift: depth 2 width 128 gives seeds +0.18866 and +0.08261, mean +0.13563, model-seed t = 2.56; depth 3 width 64 gives +0.10281 and +0.17027, mean +0.13654, t = 4.05. Both are below 4.30; the depth-2 one is below 3.182 too. Separately, FINDING 16 section 3's own second criterion (20 probe seeds, score recomputed on the same 20) reports the FAMILY at depth 3 width 64 scoring +0.0122 against a content-free control of +0.0010 and puts the family's depth-3 threshold at 64 -- which removes the depth-3 shift from the family side without touching the conventional side at all. So of the three criteria FINDING 16 itself constructed, criterion 1 gives one octave at both depths, criterion 2 gives one octave at depth 2 only, and criterion 3 (the ADOPTED one) gives one octave at depth 3 only. 'At every depth >= 2' holds under one of the three.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim must be changed to X: the threshold framing must be demoted to a criterion-conditional observation and the headline restated as a magnitude claim. Note the conventional side currently has 2 model seeds against the family's 3, so C2/C3 are underpowered against it, not decisive; but that is a reason to wait for seed 2, not a reason to publish a threshold under the retracted criterion.
objections.recommended_wording: Replace the headline clause with the criterion-free version, which is stronger and which I verified: 'At every depth >= 2 the conventional model's synthetic induction score exceeds the foldable family's by 0.13-0.60 nats at the same depth, width and (x7) parameter count; at the two cells where the family is null the family's three-model-seed score is bounded above by +0.0138 (depth 2 width 128) and +0.0106 (depth 3 width 64) at three model-seed standard errors, against conventional two-seed means of +0.1356 and +0.1365. Read as a threshold, the shift is one octave under the 5-probe-seed floor, one octave at depth 2 only under a 20-probe-seed floor, and one octave at depth 3 only under the model-seed t bar this programme adopted in FINDING 16 -- so the threshold framing is not yet a finding and the magnitude surface is.'

objections.target: "The family column is the published surface (three model seeds at depths 1-2, one at depth 3)." and the derived multipliers "6.4x at depth 3 width 128, 5.2x at depth 3 width 256" and "depth 3 width 128 averages 6.0x"
objections.objection: The parenthetical is false. All three depth-3 family seeds exist on disk, this finding's own report script already averages them, and FINDING 16 section 3 of the same RESULTS.md already published the three-seed depth-3 surface (+0.004 / +0.109 / +0.221 at widths 64/128/256 -- exactly the three-seed means). FINDING 18 therefore quotes seed-0 numbers that its own document had already superseded, and every depth-3 family figure in both tables is a single-seed figure presented in a column whose depth-1 and depth-2 entries are three-seed means. Mixing single-seed and three-seed entries in one column, unlabelled, is the 'two evaluations of the same quantity, quoted without labels' failure mode.
objections.what_I_measured: Read rung3_induction.induction_score_mean from every tf_vanilla_d{1,2,3}_w{64,128,256}_b8192_s{0,1,2}_interp3.json (27 files, all present, all 5 probe seeds) and recomputed the multipliers three ways: as published (conventional seed 0 / family seed 0 at depth 3), with the family three-seed mean, and with both sides at all available seeds.
objections.result: Depth-3 family per-seed induction: width 64 +0.00773 / +0.00326 / -0.00049 (3-seed mean +0.00350, model-seed t 1.47 -- still null, the claim gets STRONGER); width 128 +0.09736 / +0.12328 / +0.10483 (mean +0.10849); width 256 +0.16417 / +0.28460 / +0.21347 (mean +0.22074). Multipliers: depth 2 width 256 published 3.8x, all-seeds 3.50x; depth 3 width 128 published 6.4x, all-seeds 5.41x; depth 3 width 256 published 5.2x, all-seeds 3.71x. The '5.2x' is overstated by 40% and the '6.4x' by 18%. The '2-6x' band still contains all three (3.5x / 5.4x / 3.7x), so only the per-cell numbers move, not the band. Seed 0 was the LOW seed at depth 3 width 128 and width 256, which is why using it inflates the ratio -- the same 'seed 0 was the top/bottom of its range' error FINDING 16 caught in FINDING 14's route table.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives in band but the per-cell multipliers and the family column must be recomputed at three seeds
objections.recommended_wording: 'The family column is the three-model-seed surface at every depth (FINDING 16 section 3 for depth 3).' Then: 'Where both families induct the conventional score is 3.5-5.4x larger -- 3.5x at depth 2 width 256, 5.4x at depth 3 width 128, 3.7x at depth 3 width 256.' The sharpest-cell paragraph improves: at three family seeds depth 3 width 64 is +0.0035 +- 0.0024 (model-seed SE), not +0.0077.

objections.target: "the held cross-entropy tax at exactly matched parameters is **0.054-0.127 nats and grows with width**" (headline) and the six bolded YES marks in the 'conventional x7 (matched)' induction column
objections.objection: Every x7 cell has exactly ONE conventional model seed. Two consequences. (a) The bolded headline range is a one-seed-vs-one-seed paired difference quoted to three decimals in the finding's title; the body later concedes it 'should not be quoted to four decimal places from one seed', which contradicts the title. (b) More seriously, with n=1 NO model-seed criterion can be evaluated on the matched arm at all, so all six of its YES marks are probe-seed-floor verdicts at a single model seed -- the retracted criterion applied to the weakest possible sample. The matched arm is the arm the headline rests on, and it is the arm with the least evidence.
objections.what_I_measured: Counted seeds per arm in tf_baseline_std.json (x7 n_seeds = 1 at all nine cells; x4 n_seeds = 2 at all nine as of 01:29). Recomputed the x7 tax against the FAMILY THREE-SEED mean instead of family seed 0. Bounded the one-seed uncertainty using the x4 arm's observed conventional seed-to-seed held-CE spread as a proxy.
objections.result: Tax at x7 against the three-seed family mean: +0.0682 / +0.0738 / +0.0810 (depth 1), +0.0516 / +0.1031 / +0.1253 (depth 2), +0.0625 / +0.1014 / +0.1141 (depth 3) -- range 0.052-0.125 versus the published 0.054-0.127, and still monotone in width at every depth, so the seed-0 pairing is not what produces either the range or the trend. Conventional seed-to-seed held-CE spread at the x4 arm: median 0.0050, max 0.0215 (depth 2 width 128: 4.59188 vs 4.61337). Propagating that as a one-sigma-scale proxy puts the plausible matched-arm range at roughly 0.04-0.15 nats. The SIGN is safe everywhere: the smallest tax, +0.0516, is more than twice the largest observed conventional seed spread.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives in sign and in width-monotonicity; the quoted endpoints must be marked provisional and the x7 induction YES marks must be marked as single-seed probe-floor verdicts
objections.recommended_wording: Title: 'the held cross-entropy tax at exactly matched parameters is about 0.05-0.13 nats (one conventional seed per cell; sign positive at 9 of 9) and grows with width at every depth.' Add to the x7 induction columns: 'one model seed; these YES marks are probe-seed-floor verdicts and no model-seed criterion can be applied until seeds 1-2 land.'

objections.target: the two columns headed "floor" in the induction table, and "ours scores +0.0077 against a 0.0109 floor (null), the conventional model scores +0.1028 against a 0.0077 floor (13x its own noise)"
objections.objection: The two 'floor' columns are DIFFERENT STATISTICS with the same header, sitting three columns apart in one table. I could not find the table's numbers in any JSON until I worked out that the family column is the planted-oracle detectable_effect_floor_nats_3se averaged over model seeds, while the conventional columns are 3 x (probe-seed sd / sqrt(5)) -- a quantity that is not stored anywhere and has to be recomputed. The sharpest-cell sentence then compares a family power floor (0.0109) against a conventional probe standard error (0.0077) and reads the difference as the conventional detection being sharper.
objections.what_I_measured: Reverse-engineered both columns. Family: mean over the cell's model seeds of induction_power.detectable_effect_floor_nats_3se from the interp3 JSONs -- reproduces all nine published family floors to 5 decimals (e.g. depth 1 width 64: 0.00896, 0.01079, 0.00913, mean 0.00963 -> published 0.0096; depth 2 width 128: 0.00749, 0.00924, 0.01417, mean 0.01030 -> published 0.0103). Conventional: 3*sd/sqrt(5) over probe seeds -- reproduces all eighteen published conventional floors (e.g. depth 2 width 128 x4: sd 0.01688 -> 0.02265 -> published 0.0227; depth 3 width 128 x4: sd 0.02862 -> 0.03839 -> published 0.0384), whereas the detectable_effect_floor_nats_3se actually stored in those same files is 0.00811 and 0.01183. Then I re-ran the verdicts with each statistic applied to both sides.
objections.result: No verdict flips: at depth 3 width 64 the conventional score +0.1028 clears its power floor 0.01540 (6.7x) as well as its probe SE floor 0.00772 (13.3x), and the family's +0.00773 fails both its power floor 0.01093 and its probe 3-SE 0.01147. So the mismatch costs the finding nothing in outcome. It costs it in reproducibility -- none of the eighteen conventional floors can be found in the JSONs -- and the '13x its own noise' phrase is a like-against-unlike comparison that reads sharper than the like-for-like 6.7x.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives this; the table must label its two floor statistics
objections.recommended_wording: Head the columns 'planted-oracle power floor (3 SE)' and 'probe-seed 3 SE' respectively, or better, report one statistic on both sides. In the sharpest-cell sentence use the like-for-like figure: 'the conventional model scores +0.1028 against a planted-oracle power floor of 0.0154 -- 6.7x -- while ours scores +0.0077 against 0.0109 and does not clear it.'

objections.target: "The `x4` arm gives the conventional model 8-21% **fewer** total parameters"
objections.objection: Arithmetic error at the low end of the range.
objections.what_I_measured: n_params from every tfb_std4_*_s0.json and the matching tf_vanilla_*_s0.json.
objections.result: Depth 1 width 64: 573,504 vs 598,080 = 4.1% fewer, not 8%. Full range across the nine cells: 4.1 / 7.3 / 12.0 / 7.3 / 12.0 / 17.6 / 9.9 / 15.3 / 20.9 percent fewer. The correct statement is 4-21%. (The '12%' at depth 2 width 128 and the '7%' at depth 2 width 64 and the '10%' at depth 3 width 64 quoted elsewhere in the text are all correct.)
objections.survives_or_not: the claim must be changed to X: '4-21% fewer total parameters'
objections.recommended_wording: 'The x4 arm gives the conventional model 4-21% fewer total parameters, rising with both depth and width (4.1% at depth 1 width 64, 20.9% at depth 3 width 256).'

objections.target: "What survives seeding is the *sign*: positive at 8 of 8 two-seed cells at the matched arm's smaller sibling, with the single negative cell (depth 2 width 64) negative at both seeds"
objections.objection: The sentence contradicts itself: it cannot be positive at 8 of 8 and also have a negative cell among those 8. Depth 2 width 64 is one of the eight two-seed cells and its tax is negative at both seeds (-0.0077 and -0.0100).
objections.what_I_measured: Signs of the nine per-seed x4 taxes at both seeds, from the per_seed CE dictionaries in tf_baseline_std.json.
objections.result: Of the eight cells that had two seeds when the sentence was written, 7 are positive at both seeds and 1 (depth 2 width 64) is negative at both. The sign AGREES across seeds at 8 of 8. With depth 3 width 256 seed 1 now landed (family 4.20549 - conventional 4.15145 = +0.0540) it is 8 of 9 positive and 9 of 9 sign-agreeing.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives this; the sentence is mis-worded, not wrong in substance
objections.recommended_wording: 'What survives seeding is the sign: it is reproduced at 9 of 9 two-seed cells -- positive at 8 of them and negative at both seeds of the ninth (depth 2 width 64, the arm where the conventional model is also 7% smaller).'

objections.target: "it is reported now because the induction gaps are an order of magnitude larger than either family's across-seed spread"
objections.objection: This is the justification for publishing before replication, and it is false for the conventional family at exactly the two cells the headline depends on. It was true when written (only the family's spread was known); it stopped being true when conventional seed 1 landed, and the seed-1 section was appended to the same finding without revisiting the justification.
objections.what_I_measured: Between-family gap divided by each family's across-model-seed standard deviation, at the two threshold-defining cells.
objections.result: Depth 2 width 128: gap 0.1390 nats; family sd 0.00987 -> 14x (true); conventional sd 0.07499 -> 1.9x (false). Depth 3 width 64: gap 0.1330; family sd 0.00412 -> 32x (true); conventional sd 0.04770 -> 2.8x (false). The corresponding two-sample Welch t between families are 2.61 (depth 2 width 128, n = 2 vs 3) and 3.93 (depth 3 width 64).
objections.survives_or_not: the claim must be changed to X: the gap is an order of magnitude larger than the FAMILY's across-seed spread, and 1.9-2.8x the conventional model's own near-threshold spread
objections.recommended_wording: '...because the induction gaps are 14-32x the foldable family's across-seed spread. The conventional model's own near-threshold spread is much larger (its two seeds differ by 2.3x at depth 2 width 128), so the between-family Welch t at the threshold cells is 2.6 and 3.9, not an order of magnitude -- this is exactly why seed 2 is required before the threshold clause is asserted.'

objections.target: "Buying foldability at depth 3 width 64 does not cost 6% of a nat -- it costs induction entirely." and "The depth-3 width-64 cell is the sharpest single comparison in the programme"
objections.objection: 'Entirely' is a null asserted with a detector that FINDING 16 has already shown is at the edge of its power there. FINDING 16 section 3 reports the family's width-64 cells at 20 probe seeds scoring +0.0122 (depth 3) and +0.0221 (depth 4) against a depth-matched content-free control of +0.0010, and states in terms: 'The width-64 cells are not zero ... they are small.' FINDING 18 reasserts the null at that cell from a 5-probe-seed measurement without re-running the 20-probe-seed check that produced the qualification -- the standing failure mode about retractions travelling with the METHOD.
objections.what_I_measured: The second, independent detector that both families already carry: natural_induction.ORDER_ONLY_patch_swap, an order-only swap patch on HELD NATURAL TEXT, present in every family interp3 JSON and every conventional induction JSON.
objections.result: At depth 3 width 64 the family scores +0.0534 (three seeds: 0.0546 / 0.0504 / 0.0551) against the conventional x4's +0.1547 (0.1380 / 0.1713) -- a factor of 2.9, not a null. Referenced to the depth-1 width-64 baseline of the same detector (family +0.0407, conventional x4 +0.0431), which is a depth that CANNOT induct, the excesses are +0.013 (family) and +0.111 (conventional), a factor of 8.6. The natural detector agrees with the synthetic one in sign at all nine cells and in ordering at all nine, so it corroborates the direction and the size of the gap -- but it does NOT support 'entirely'.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives in substance (the gap at that cell is real and large on two independent detectors) but 'costs induction entirely' must go
objections.recommended_wording: 'Buying foldability at depth 3 width 64 does not cost 6% of a nat -- on the synthetic battery it costs 0.133 nats of induction score, taking the family from an 8.6x excess over its depth-1 control down to a 1.3x one on the natural-text order-only detector. The family's residual there is small but not zero (+0.0122 at 20 probe seeds in FINDING 16 against a +0.0010 content-free control); the honest statement is a bound, not a null.'

objections.target: the whole section "### Held cross-entropy: the tax, and what it costs to pay it"
objections.objection: Standing failure mode added to this README the previous day: 'Every CE number must carry its split, its context length and its token count.' The section heading says only 'held cross-entropy'. tf_baseline_std.json does carry it ('All CE at T=512 on held rows [0:1500]'), and the earlier FINDING 18 preamble does not repeat it, so a reader of RESULTS.md alone cannot tell which of this programme's two held evaluations (rung5_ladder._model_ce at context 256 vs final_held_ce at context 512) is being quoted -- the exact ambiguity that cost the depth-3 slice 33% of its published margin.
objections.what_I_measured: Traced the numbers: all eighteen conventional and all nine family CE values in the table are run.final_held_ce, i.e. TR.eval_held on held rows [0:1500] at T=512. I confirmed by exact match against the source JSONs (108-number recomputation, one round-tie).
objections.result: The numbers are the right ones and are consistent across both sides; only the label is missing.
objections.recommended_wording: Add under the heading: 'Held cross-entropy in nats/token, tf_train.eval_held on held rows [0:1500] at context T=512 (768,000 predicted tokens), the training-protocol number -- final_held_ce, not the rung-5 ladder's context-256 evaluation. Both families share the tokenizer, so nats are directly comparable; bits/byte = nats / (ln2 x 3.755).'

objections.target: the seed-1 table row "| 3 | 256 | ... | training | YES / -- | +0.0717 | -- |"
objections.objection: Standing failure mode: 'never report from an agent's in-flight artifacts'. The chain is still running (tf_baseline_chain.sh, pid 985122, now on stage 2's x7 seeds), and this cell completed at 01:29 UTC, three minutes after RESULTS.md was last written. One published cell is already stale. Everything else I checked against the current JSONs still matches, so the exposure is one cell -- but the finding is being written from a live chain and will keep going stale until the chain declares final.
objections.what_I_measured: Compared RESULTS.md's mtime (01:26) with the chain log and the current on-disk values; re-read tf_baseline_std.json after the 01:29 report rebuild.
objections.result: Depth 3 width 256 conventional x4 seed 1 has landed: held CE 4.15145, induction +0.78712 (clears its own floors), tax against family seed 1 = 4.20549 - 4.15145 = +0.0540. It fills the table's only gap and does not change any verdict: the two-seed x4 mean at that cell becomes +0.81972 and the detect verdict is 9 of 9 rather than 8 of 8. Nothing else on disk disagrees with the published tables.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives this and is strengthened; the row must be filled in

objections.target: "That biases *against* the conventional model, so it makes every number above a **lower bound** on the tax. It cannot explain the gap away -- it can only widen it."
objections.objection: The direction is plausible but it is asserted, not measured, and 'it can only widen it' is a monotonicity claim about an unmeasured hyper-parameter. Both arms that would price it (the no-QK-norm control at depth 2 width 128 x 3 seeds, and the full-length lr 0.01/0.04 bound) are stages 3 and 4 of a chain currently on stage 2, i.e. unrun. A softmax temperature has an interior optimum: if 1/sqrt(16) with query/key RMSNorm happened to sit near or past it, correcting it could move the CE either way. I therefore went looking for the opposite direction -- anything held fixed from the family's history that FLATTERS the conventional model.
objections.what_I_measured: Read tf_baseline_std.py against tf_model.py line by line for asymmetries: weight init (both nn.Linear default, both zero-init residual-branch output projections, both embedding N(0, 0.02)), optimiser split, warmup/cosine/clip, rotary tables, logit soft cap, tied embedding, per-head query/key RMSNorm, head_dim, bias count, corpus, data order (C6 sha256 shared), eval, and dropout (there is none in either file, so the shim's model.eval() is a no-op and creates no asymmetry). Then I measured the one asymmetry I could quantify: what the x4 -> x7 step actually buys the conventional model, per parameter, against the family's own parameter-to-loss conversion rate.
objections.result: Two things. (1) I found no init, data, optimiser or evaluation asymmetry -- every one of those is symmetric, and C1/C6/C7 close the harness and data-drift routes at exactly 0.0. So the lower-bound argument has no counterexample I can find in the code. (2) But there IS a real, unstated structural asymmetry in what 'matched' means. The family spends 12W^2 on three feed-forward matrices at hidden 4W; the conventional x7 arm spends 14W^2 on two matrices at hidden 7W. At matched parameters the conventional model therefore gets a 1.75x WIDER hidden layer, and the x4 arm is the one that matches hidden width. The two arms bracket rather than one being 'the' match. Quantitatively the x4 -> x7 step buys the conventional model 0.033-0.062 nats for 24.6k-1.18M extra body parameters (1.33 / 0.47 / 0.11 / 1.26 / 0.25 / 0.07 / 0.74 / 0.15 / 0.04 nats per million body parameters), against the family's own width-doubling conversion of about 0.18 nats per million body parameters at depth 2 -- i.e. the same order, with no sign that expansion 7 is an anomalous sweet spot. I cannot rule it out without training, which I am not permitted to do.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives as a plausible expectation but must stop being stated as a certainty, and the bracketing point should be made explicit
objections.recommended_wording: 'The softmax temperature is unpriced and the no-QK-norm and learning-rate arms have not run. The expected direction is against the conventional model, which would make these numbers a lower bound on the tax, but that is an expectation about an interior optimum, not a measurement, and it will be one until stages 3 and 4 land. Separately: the two arms bracket rather than one being definitive. x4 matches the feed-forward HIDDEN WIDTH (4W both) and gives the conventional model 4-21% fewer parameters; x7 matches PARAMETERS exactly (body and total, to the integer, at 9 of 9 cells) and gives it a 1.75x wider hidden layer. There is no allocation that matches both.'

objections.target: control C4 and the commensurability of the two families' induction numbers
objections.objection: The line of attack I was asked to press hardest turned out to be the finding's strongest point, so I am recording it as a negative result rather than an objection. The worry was that the conventional numbers come from tf_baseline_probe.py while the family numbers come from tf_interp3.py, and that C4 validates only one cell.
objections.what_I_measured: Compared the two call sites (tf_interp3.py line 1287 vs tf_baseline_probe.py line 67), the battery signature and defaults (tf_interp.induction_battery, n_seq=48, L=96, probe seeds range(5) on both sides), the shim fields, and the synthetic-data construction; then checked which cells C4 covers and whether the family cells in FINDING 18's table go through the validated path.
objections.result: Commensurable, and more tightly than the finding claims. Both sides call the identical function with identical defaults and 5 probe seeds; the battery's sequences are built from a CPU generator seeded only by the probe seed and a unigram taken from load_split(V,'train',4000,tok=cfg.tok), and both families have V=8192 and tok='bpe' -- so the two families are scored on BIT-IDENTICAL synthetic inputs, not merely on statistically matched ones. C4's checked cell (tf_vanilla_d2_w256_b8192_s0, abs_diff exactly 0.0) IS one of the nine family cells in FINDING 18's table, and every other family cell in the table comes from the same rung3_induction code path in the same script, so the validation transfers by code identity rather than by extrapolation. Neither model has any dropout or normalisation with train/eval behaviour, so the shim's model.eval() is a no-op. I found no probe-code difference of any kind.
objections.survives_or_not: the claim survives this completely; if anything the finding undersells C4
objections.recommended_wording: 'C4 is stronger than a reproduction check: because the battery's synthetic sequences depend only on the probe seed, the vocabulary and the tokenizer -- all identical across the two families -- both families are scored on bit-identical inputs, and C4 confirms the shim reproduces a published foldable score at abs_diff 0.0 on one of the nine family cells in the table below.'

disagreements.cell: depth 1 width 128, tax at the x4 arm
disagreements.note: 5.14244-style source values give 4.81940 - 4.79455 = 0.024850 exactly -- a round-half tie. Cosmetic; either printed value is defensible.

arithmetic_check.what_was_covered: All 54 entries of the cross-entropy table (family CE, conventional x4 CE, tax x4, parameter ratio, conventional x7 CE, tax x7 at all nine cells) and all 54 entries of the induction table (family score, family floor, x4 score, x4 floor, x7 score, x7 floor at all nine cells), each recomputed from tf_vanilla_*.json / tf_vanilla_*_interp3.json / tfb_std*.json / tfb_std*_induction.json. Also checked and found correct: the 3.8x / 6.4x / 5.2x multipliers as computed from the stated seed selection, the 13x noise ratio (0.1028/0.00772 = 13.3), the 66% seed-1 increase (1.656), the 2.3x fall (2.284) and 1.7x rise, the 14% and 11% away-from-threshold changes, the 3.5x and 6.0x two-seed averages, all nine seed-1 taxes, the 18W^2+W vs 12W^2+W body formulas, the 590,080 body-parameter figure at depth 2 width 128, and the width-monotonicity of the matched tax at all three depths. Found INCORRECT: the '8-21% fewer parameters' range (O5, true range 4.1-20.9%) and the 'positive at 8 of 8' count (O6, true count 7 of 8 positive / 8 of 8 sign-agreeing).

things_I_could_not_check_and_why: Whether a tuned softmax temperature closes any of the gap. This requires training, which the review brief forbids, and the no-QK-norm arm (chain stage 3) and the full-length learning-rate arms (stage 4) have not run -- the chain was on stage 2 (x7 seed 1) throughout this review. The finding's lower-bound argument therefore rests on an unmeasured monotonicity (O11).

Whether the conventional model's model-seed t values at the two threshold-defining cells clear 3.182 or 4.30 with three seeds. Seed 2 of the x4 arm is chain stage 5 and has not started. The current two-seed values are 2.56 (depth 2 width 128) and 4.05 (depth 3 width 64), i.e. both could land on either side. This is the single largest open item and it is what O1 turns on.

FINDING 16's second criterion (20-probe-seed floor with the score recomputed on the same 20 probe seeds) applied to the CONVENTIONAL checkpoints. Recomputing it would mean re-running the battery at 20 probe seeds on 27 checkpoints; the GPU is owned by the baseline chain and the brief forbids competing for it, and on CPU this is hours. I used FINDING 16's own published 20-probe-seed FAMILY numbers instead, which is enough to show that criterion removes the depth-3 half of the shift from the family side, but I could not confirm what it does to the conventional side.

Whether the induction battery's synthetic distribution (i.i.d. unigram draws, L=96 repeated) is architecture-neutral between a softmax attention and an unnormalised two-branch product whose row mass is not normalised (tf_model.py line 563: pat = (s1*s2).masked_fill(~mask, 0.0), no row normalisation). A length-dependent scale difference between the families on out-of-distribution synthetic text is conceivable and I could not isolate it without training length-matched controls. I did the next best thing -- checked the independent natural-text detector, which agrees in sign at 9 of 9 cells and in ordering at 9 of 9 (O8) -- so if this bias exists it does not reverse anything.

Whether expansion 7 is an unusually favourable operating point for a GELU feed-forward net in some way beyond parameter count. Settling it needs an expansion sweep (5, 6, 7, 8) at fixed parameters, which is training. The per-parameter conversion rate I could measure (0.04-1.33 nats per million body parameters for the x4->x7 step, against about 0.18 for the family's own width doubling at depth 2) shows nothing anomalous but does not rule it out.
what_would_settle_the_biggest_open_objec: Run x4 seed 2 at depth 2 width 128 and depth 3 width 64 -- the two cells that define the one-octave shift, about 12 minutes of GPU between them at the observed chain rate -- and then recompute the threshold table under the model-seed criterion FINDING 16 ADOPTED (one-sample t over model seeds against t(2) > 3.182, the same bar that finding used, and against the t > 4.30 hard-coded in tf_baseline_report.py). The current two-seed t values are 2.56 at depth 2 width 128 and 4.05 at depth 3 width 64; with the third seed both become well-defined three-seed t(2) statistics directly comparable to the family's 18.79 / 14.08 / 6.32 / 1.47 / -0.59. If depth 2 width 128 then clears 3.182, the 'at every depth >= 2' clause is earned under the programme's own adopted criterion and O1 collapses to a labelling fix; if it does not, the headline must become 'one octave at depth 3, and a large but not-yet-separated magnitude gap at depth 2'. Everything else in the finding -- the cross-entropy tax, the exact parameter matching, the depth-1 negative control, the probe commensurability -- is already settled and does not depend on the answer.
